items.summary: View CSAF Summary On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. The following versions of Siemens Desigo, Gridscale are affected: Desigo CC family V8 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-111497) Desigo CC family V9 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-111497) Gridscale X DSA vers:intdot/>=5.3|<5.4 (CVE-2026-111497) Gridscale X PSS®E vers:intdot/<36.8.0 (CVE-2026-111497) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 9.8 Siemens Desigo CC family V8 1 Vulnerability Out-of-bounds Write Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Information Technology Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-111497 A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1. Read More 4 Affected Products Desigo CC family V8 Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected Remediations Vendor fix Install the latest .NET security updates via Windows Update. Desigo CC family V9 Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected Remediations Vendor fix Install the latest .NET security updates via Windows Update. Gridscale X DSA >= V5.3 < V5.4 Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V5.4 or later version Gridscale X PSS®E < V36.8.0 Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update to V36.8.0 or later version Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 9.8 CRITICAL CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H View CVE Details Acknowledgments Siemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA. General Recommendations Operators of critical power systems (e.g. TSOs or DSOs) worldwide are usually required by regulations to build resilience into the power grids by applying multi-level redundant secondary protection schemes. It is therefore recommended that the operators check whether appropriate resilient protection measures are in place. The risk of cyber incidents impacting the grid's reliability can thus be minimized by virtue of the grid design. Siemens strongly recommends applying the provided security updates using the corresponding tooling and documented procedures made available with the product. If supported by the product, an automated means to apply the security updates across multiple product instances may be used. Siemens strongly recommends prior validation of any security update before being applied, and supervision by trained staff of the update process in the target environment. As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access with appropriate mechanisms (e.g. firewalls, segmentation, VPN). It is advised to configure the environment according to our operational guidelines in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment. Recommended security guidelines can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/gridsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advis

items.summary: View CSAF Summary Palo Alto Networks has published information on vulnerabilities in PAN-OS related to PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. This advisory lists the related Siemens Industrial products affected by these vulnerabilities. Customers are advised to consult and implement the workarounds provided in Palo Alto Networks' upstream security notifications. The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 are affected: RUGGEDCOM APE1808 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 9.8 Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 1 Vulnerability Use After Free Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-109618 PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE). Read More 1 Affected Product RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (10.2 All, 11.1 All, 11.2 All, 12.1 All, 12.2 All) Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Upgrade to corresponding available PAN-OS version. Contact customer support to receive additional patch and update information. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE). items.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have found that lookalike domains masquerading as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being used to serve ClickFix-style lures, browser-hijacking malware, and a set of extensions that hijack user searches.

Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose.

The Threat Research team at Material Security spotted the campaign and has since taken down hundreds of attacker domains in an effort the team calls Operation CloudFire.
